newsitem.title: VENEZUELA: Venezuela to pump 3.245 mln bpd oil in 97 - source.
newsitem.headline: Venezuela to pump 3.245 mln bpd oil in 97 - source.

text.p: Venezuela's state-owned oil company Petroleos de Venezuela (PDVSA) plans to pump an average 3.245 million barrels per day (bpd) of crude oil and condensate in 1997, rising to 3.652 million in 1998, a source at the company said on Monday.
The source, who saw official figures but asked to remain anonymous, said PDVSA planned to up crude and condensate production to average 4.097 million bpd in 1999.
Current condensate production runs at less than 100,000 bpd.

The figures do not include natural gas liquids or orimulsion, the source said. NGL production was forecast to be 197,000 bpd in 1998 and 215,000 bpd in 1999, while orimulsion output would rise from 71,000 bpd in 1996 to about 86,000 bpd next year, he said.
In its 1996 annual results, PDVSA said its crude and condensate production capacity stood at 3.416 million bpd.

The accelerating production forecast conforms to the company's plan to double output in ten years, but conflicts with the country's official output quota set by the Organisation for Petroleum Exporting Countries (OPEC) of 2.359 million bpd.
Venezuela's Energy and Mines Minister Erwin Arrieta is due to meet other OPEC ministers in Vienna on Wednesday to discuss world demand and supply and set its members' quotas.

Although the minister has come out in favour of no change in the organisation's output ceiling, he said last week he would demand a reply to his suggestion that OPEC change its strategy towards the markets.
PDVSA president Luis Giusti has been arguing for OPEC to drop the quota system altogether in favour of a policy to gain market share.
